title: Pierogi Ruskie
description: Dumplings filled with potato and twarog, boiled and then fried in butter with onions. The dough is worked warm and rested, which is what keeps it from tearing.
notes: Freeze them raw on a tray before bagging, and boil from frozen. They do not survive being stacked wet.

ingredients.name: onions
ingredients.note: one for the filling, one to serve

steps.text: Mix the flour and salt with the warm water and melted butter, then knead until smooth and elastic.

steps.tip: Unrested dough springs back while you are trying to fill it and the seals fail.

steps.text: Fry one diced onion in half the butter until deep golden.
Mash the fried onion into the riced potatoes and twarog with the white pepper and plenty of salt, and let it cool completely.
steps.tip: Taste it and over-season slightly — the dough around it is unsalted.

steps.text: Roll the dough thin and cut rounds, keeping the offcuts covered as you go.
Place a spoonful of filling on each round, fold, and pinch the edge firmly all the way along.
steps.tip: Wet fingers make the seal worse, not better. Dry, firm pressure holds.

steps.text: Boil in well-salted water in batches until they float, then give them another minute.
Fry the remaining sliced onion in the rest of the butter and toss the drained pierogi through it.
